audience: Researchers comparing payout mechanics, not personal tax planning

tax_info_requirement.expiration_rule: Existing forms may expire at the end of the third full calendar year after signing; review annually and resubmit on material changes.

payer_withholding_cases.payee: Non-US creator with accepted tax information
payer_withholding_cases.applicability: Conditional on country/residence, beneficial owner/entity type and any accepted tax treaty documentation

payer_withholding_cases.payee: Non-US business-account payee with no valid information
payer_withholding_cases.applicability: YouTube documents this as a default withholding case; not a substitute for determining actual account classification

payer_withholding_cases.payee: Individual-account payee without required tax information
payer_withholding_cases.applicability: Google warns of backup withholding on total worldwide earnings when required tax info is missing

payer_withholding_cases.payee: US creator with valid tax information
payer_withholding_cases.applicability: YouTube states it does not withhold U.S. taxes for U.S. creators who provided valid info; separate income-tax liability may still apply

disallowed_model_shortcuts: Do not apply any U.S.-viewer withholding percentage to worldwide native earnings unless the documented payee case explicitly permits that base.
Do not subtract taxes twice when computing payout balance and later after-tax cash proceeds.
Do not treat Google payment withholding as comprehensive tax liability, tax advice or a country-wide applicable rate.
Do not infer treaty benefits from language, audience geography, name or creator's approximate location.
Do not identify the creator's tax form from a platform or country label; tax classification and individual circumstances govern.
No personally identifying tax forms, numbers or financial account data may enter the public study.
